subject: Hosted API: token runway & TPS waterfall (post-demo)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Li <harper@aureus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Hosted API: token runway & TPS waterfall (post-demo)

Hi Harper — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and very targeted asks so we can turn this into a clean pricing + ops proposal: 

Recap (3 lines)
- You’re planning to embed multi-turn assistant flows into the product, weighted toward responses (longer completions).
- Expected ramp: POC in July, GA in Q4.
- Primary region: US-east, with global read-only traffic later.

We need confirmation on a few traffic and budget points to size the hosted pricing: 
1) Monthly token range: please confirm a low/expected/high monthly token estimate for months 1–6. We typically model an 80/120/160M example but want your numbers.
2) Avg tokens per interaction: what’s a typical prompt + completion token split? (e.g., 200 prompt / 600 completion = 800 tokens/request)
3) Peak TPS shape: confirm sustained peak (60s–5m windows) and any extreme microbursts (10–30s) — examples: sustained 180 TPS, microbursts to 300 TPS.
4) Budget target: what dollar per 1M tokens are you hoping for (range)? Helpful for committing to a band vs. on-demand.
5) Procurement/security checklist: point person + must-have controls (SOC2, SSO, data residency).

High-level guidance from our side (ballpark, not formal):
- For the traffic shapes you described we typically recommend a commit band for predictable unit cost + burst buffer for sudden spikes.
- With prefix/KV caching we often see 10–30% token reduction for repeated assistant prompts (depends on rewrite).
- For 100–140M/mo and average ~700–900 tokens/req, a conservative hosted estimate sits between $9–$13 / 1M tokens depending on term and burst guarantees.

Next steps I propose:
- Harper: reply with the two numbers above (monthly low/expected/high and the average tokens/req + peak TPS windows).
- Ben/Karthik: we’ll run a quick unit-econ sketch once Harper confirms.
- I’ll attach a one-sheet MAP + an example pricing cadence for commit bands. If it looks reasonable we’ll follow with a 30-min technical sync (engineer + infra).

Attaching: aureus-map.xlsx (fill the traffic table), redwood-hosted-pricing-proposal.pdf (example bands).

Thanks — Olg

--
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
From: Harper Li <harper@aureus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@aureus.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 18:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: token runway & TPS waterfall (post-demo)

Thanks Olga — great session. Answers below inline.

Monthly tokens (months 1–6): low 90M / expected 115M / high 140M. This assumes steady growth after POC and increased prompt length as we broaden features.

Avg tokens per interaction: we’re currently seeing ~720 tokens per user interaction on average (prompt ~180 / completion ~540). Some of our longer generative flows go to ~1.4k tokens but are <5% of requests.

Peak TPS shape: typical sustained morning peak ~170–200 TPS for ~3–6 minutes; we see microbursts up to ~280–320 TPS for 10–25s during product launches. Our 99th percentile across all users is closer to 240 TPS.

Budget target: procurement is aiming for a $11–$13 / 1M token window for hosted API, ideally with a 12-month commit if the unit economics work out.

Procurement/security: procurement@aureus.ai (CC’d) will start a standard vendor form. Must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/SCIM, clear data retention controls, and ability to sign an SLA with uptime and latency targets.

If you can sketch pricing bands that hit $11–$13 for a 12-month commit at 110–120M/mo that’ll help accelerate procurement.

Best,
Harper

Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: token runway & TPS waterfall (post-demo)

Looping in Karthik to confirm economics and burst guidance. Quick thought from pricing: given Harper’s 115M expected and peak shapes, we should propose two paths:

1) 12-month commit: 120M/mo at $10.50 / 1M tokens + included burst buffer (up to 300 TPS for 5 minutes).
2) On-demand with tiered unit pricing: $13 / 1M for first 50M, $11.50 / 1M for next 100M, automatic burst throttles (when burst >300 TPS we can route to a compatible lower-cost model or degrade gracefully).

Karthik — can you validate the burst SLA feasibility and whether prefix caching could get them to the lower end of their target? I’ll draft a short MAP that shows monthly savings by band.

-Ben

Harper — appreciate the detailed numbers, that’s exactly what we needed. Next steps and what you can expect from us this week: 

1) Pricing sketch: Ben/Karthik will send a 2-option pricing sketch (commit vs on-demand) by EOD Tue 6/22. Expect the commit path to sit around $10–$11 / 1M for 120M/mo with an explicit burst buffer for short microbursts.
2) Technical sync: propose Wed 6/23 or Fri 6/25 for a 30-min session (engineer + infra) to validate the 99th/peak shapes and uplift/rollback behavior under burst. Please share which day/time works.
3) Procurement: Olga will loop legal ops for SOC2 + SLA templates; procurement contact noted.

I’ve attached the MAP workbook (aureus-map.xlsx — please fill the traffic sheet) and a short PDF that shows our commit band example. Also dropping a HubSpot link to the deal so your procurement team can see the MAP and docs: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/2347

If the $11–$13 window is firm on procurement’s end we’ll prioritize the commit band scenario that lands inside it. If they’re flexible, the on-demand tiering can be less complex to stand up.

Thanks — Olga
